notes:
Basics

  • Vector $\vec a = x\hat i + y\hat j + z\hat k$; magnitude $|\vec a| = \sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}$; unit vector $\hat a = \vec a/|\vec a|$.
  • Direction cosines $(l,m,n)$ of $\vec a$: $l = x/|\vec a|$, $m=y/|\vec a|$, $n=z/|\vec a|$, with $l^2+m^2+n^2=1$. Direction ratios are any numbers proportional to $l,m,n$.
  • Position vector of the point dividing $AB$ in ratio $m:n$ internally: $\dfrac{m\vec b + n\vec a}{m+n}$; externally: $\dfrac{m\vec b - n\vec a}{m-n}$. Midpoint: $\dfrac{\vec a+\vec b}{2}$.

Scalar (Dot) Product

  • $\vec a\cdot\vec b = |\vec a||\vec b|\cos\theta = a_1b_1+a_2b_2+a_3b_3$.
  • $\vec a\cdot\vec b = 0 \Leftrightarrow \vec a \perp \vec b$ (both nonzero). $\hat i\cdot\hat i=\hat j\cdot\hat j=\hat k\cdot\hat k=1$; $\hat i\cdot\hat j=\hat j\cdot\hat k=\hat k\cdot\hat i=0$.
  • Projection of $\vec a$ on $\vec b$ $= \dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec b|}$. Useful identity: $|\vec a+\vec b|^2 = |\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2+2\vec a\cdot\vec b$.

Vector (Cross) Product

  • $\vec a\times\vec b = |\vec a||\vec b|\sin\theta\,\hat n$, computed as the determinant $\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\a_1&a_2&a_3\\b_1&b_2&b_3\end{vmatrix}$.
  • $\vec a\times\vec b = \vec 0 \Leftrightarrow \vec a \parallel \vec b$ (both nonzero). $\hat i\times\hat j=\hat k$, $\hat j\times\hat k=\hat i$, $\hat k\times\hat i=\hat j$ (cyclic); anticommutative: $\vec a\times\vec b = -\vec b\times\vec a$.
  • Area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides $\vec a,\vec b$ $= |\vec a\times\vec b|$; area of the triangle $= \dfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b|$.

Scalar Triple Product

  • $[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c] = \vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)$, equal to the determinant of the three rows of components; it gives the volume of the parallelepiped with co-terminous edges $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$.
  • $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ are coplanar $\Leftrightarrow [\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c] = 0$.

Exam tip

KCET typically sets 3–4 questions from this chapter: magnitude/unit vector, dot product & angle between two vectors, cross product & area of a triangle, and a coplanarity or section-formula question. The identity $|\vec a+\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2+2\vec a\cdot\vec b$ shortcuts most 'find the resultant' problems.

questions.q: The magnitude of $\vec a = 2\hat i - 3\hat j + 6\hat k$ is
questions.trick: $|\vec a|=\sqrt{\text{sum of squares of components}}$ — always.

questions.q: The unit vector along $3\hat i + 4\hat j$ is
questions.explanation: $|3\hat i+4\hat j| = \sqrt{9+16} = 5$, so the unit vector is $\dfrac{3\hat i+4\hat j}{5}$.
questions.trick: 3-4-5 triangle: magnitude is 5 instantly, so unit vector is $\vec a/5$.

questions.q: If $\hat a$ and $\hat b$ are unit vectors with angle $60^\circ$ between them, then $\hat a\cdot\hat b =$
questions.explanation: $\hat a\cdot\hat b = |\hat a||\hat b|\cos60^\circ = 1\times1\times0.5 = 0.5$.
questions.trick: For unit vectors, $\hat a\cdot\hat b=\cos\theta$ directly — no magnitudes needed.

questions.q: If $\vec a = \hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b = \hat i-\hat j+\hat k$, then $\vec a\cdot\vec b =$
questions.trick: Dot product: multiply matching components, then sum them.

questions.q: The angle between $\vec a = \hat i+\hat j$ and $\vec b = \hat j+\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec a\cdot\vec b = 1$, $|\vec a|=|\vec b|=\sqrt2$, so $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$, giving $\theta = 60^\circ$.
questions.trick: $\cos\theta=(\vec a\cdot\vec b)/(|\vec a||\vec b|)$ — compute all three quickly.

questions.q: $(\hat i \times \hat j)\cdot \hat k =$
questions.explanation: $\hat i\times\hat j = \hat k$, so $(\hat i\times\hat j)\cdot\hat k = \hat k\cdot\hat k = 1$.
questions.trick: $\hat i\times\hat j=\hat k$ identity, then $\hat k\cdot\hat k=1$ — memorise the cyclic triad.

questions.q: If $\vec a = 2\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$ and $\vec b = \hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$, then $\vec a\times\vec b =$
questions.explanation: $\vec a\times\vec b = \hat i(1\cdot3-(-1)\cdot2) - \hat j(2\cdot3-(-1)\cdot1) + \hat k(2\cdot2-1\cdot1) = 5\hat i-7\hat j+3\hat k$.
questions.trick: Cross product = determinant of $\hat i,\hat j,\hat k$ rows; expand along the top.

questions.q: The area of the triangle with adjacent sides $\hat i+\hat j$ and $\hat i-\hat j$ is
questions.explanation: $(\hat i+\hat j)\times(\hat i-\hat j) = -2\hat k$, magnitude $2$; area of triangle $= \dfrac12(2) = 1$.
questions.trick: Cross first, then halve the magnitude for triangle area (not parallelogram).

questions.q: If $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are nonzero vectors and $\vec a \times \vec b = \vec 0$, then $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are
questions.explanation: The cross product vanishes only when $\sin\theta = 0$, i.e. $\theta = 0^\circ$ or $180^\circ$, so the vectors are parallel.
questions.trick: Zero cross product $\Rightarrow$ parallel vectors, since $\sin\theta=0$.

questions.q: If $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are nonzero vectors and $\vec a\cdot\vec b = 0$, then $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are
questions.explanation: The dot product vanishes only when $\cos\theta=0$, i.e. $\theta = 90^\circ$, so the vectors are perpendicular.
questions.trick: Zero dot product $\Rightarrow$ perpendicular vectors, since $\cos\theta=0$.

questions.q: The projection of $\vec a = \hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ on $\vec b = 2\hat i-2\hat j+\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec a\cdot\vec b = 2-2+1 = 1$, $|\vec b| = \sqrt{4+4+1}=3$, so the projection $= \dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec b|} = \dfrac13$.
questions.trick: Projection of $\vec a$ on $\vec b$ is $(\vec a\cdot\vec b)/|\vec b|$, divide by $|\vec b|$ only.

questions.q: $\hat i \cdot (\hat j \times \hat k) =$
questions.explanation: $\hat j\times\hat k = \hat i$, so $\hat i\cdot(\hat j\times\hat k) = \hat i\cdot\hat i = 1$.
questions.trick: $\hat j\times\hat k=\hat i$, so $\hat i\cdot(\hat j\times\hat k)=1$ — basis triple product.

questions.q: The vectors $\vec a = \hat i+\hat j+\hat k$, $\vec b = \hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$ and $\vec c = 2\hat i+3\hat j+4\hat k$ are
questions.explanation: The scalar triple product $\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&3\\2&3&4\end{vmatrix} = 1(8-9)-1(4-6)+1(3-4) = -1+2-1 = 0$, so the vectors are coplanar.
questions.trick: Coplanar test: the $3\times3$ scalar triple product determinant equals zero.

questions.q: The direction cosines of the vector $\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ are
questions.explanation: $|\hat i+\hat j+\hat k| = \sqrt3$, so each direction cosine is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$.
questions.trick: Divide each component by the magnitude to get direction cosines.

questions.q: If $A(1,2,3)$ and $B(4,6,3)$, the magnitude of $\vec{AB}$ is
questions.trick: $\vec{AB}=B-A$; then magnitude is $\sqrt{\text{sum of squares}}$.

questions.q: The point dividing the line joining $A(2,3,4)$ and $B(4,5,6)$ internally in the ratio $2:1$ is
questions.trick: Internal division ratio $m{:}n$: point $=(m\vec b+n\vec a)/(m+n)$.

questions.q: If $|\vec a|=3$, $|\vec b|=4$ and $\vec a\perp\vec b$, then $|\vec a+\vec b| =$
questions.explanation: $|\vec a+\vec b|^2 = |\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2+2\vec a\cdot\vec b = 9+16+0=25$, so $|\vec a+\vec b|=5$.
questions.trick: Perpendicular vectors: $|\vec a+\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2$, like Pythagoras.

questions.q: If $|\vec a|=|\vec b|=1$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec b=0$, then $|\vec a-2\vec b| =$
questions.explanation: $|\vec a-2\vec b|^2 = |\vec a|^2+4|\vec b|^2-4\vec a\cdot\vec b = 1+4-0=5$, so $|\vec a-2\vec b|=\sqrt5$.
questions.trick: Expand $|\vec a-2\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+4|\vec b|^2-4\vec a\cdot\vec b$, use $\vec a\cdot\vec b=0$.

questions.q: If $\vec a = 2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b = \hat i+\hat j-2\hat k$, then $\vec a+\vec b =$
questions.explanation: Adding components: $(2+1)\hat i+(-1+1)\hat j+(1-2)\hat k = 3\hat i - \hat k$.
questions.trick: Add or subtract vectors component-wise: $\hat i,\hat j,\hat k$ terms separately.

questions.q: If $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c = \vec 0$, $|\vec a|=3$, $|\vec b|=5$, $|\vec c|=7$, then $\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a =$
questions.explanation: $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2=0=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2+|\vec c|^2+2(\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a) = 83+2S$, so $S=-83/2$.
questions.trick: $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2=0$ expands to sum of squares $+2(\text{dot terms})$ — solve for the sum.

questions.q: The magnitude of $\vec a = 3\hat i - 4\hat j + 12\hat k$ is
questions.trick: 3-4-12 form a Pythagorean-style triple: $\sqrt{9+16+144}=13$ instantly.

questions.q: The unit vector along $-\hat i+\hat j$ is
questions.explanation: $|-\hat i+\hat j|=\sqrt{1+1}=\sqrt2$, so the unit vector is $\dfrac{-\hat i+\hat j}{\sqrt2}$.
questions.trick: Magnitude of $(-1,1,0)$-type vectors is $\sqrt2$ — a standard shortcut.

questions.q: If $|\vec a|=5$, $|\vec b|=12$ and $\vec a\perp\vec b$, then $|\vec a+\vec b|=$
questions.explanation: $|\vec a+\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2+2\vec a\cdot\vec b=25+144+0=169$, so $|\vec a+\vec b|=13$.
questions.trick: 5-12-13 triple: perpendicular vectors add via Pythagoras to give 13.

questions.q: $\hat i\cdot\hat i+\hat j\cdot\hat j+\hat k\cdot\hat k=$
questions.explanation: Each term equals 1 since $\hat i,\hat j,\hat k$ are unit vectors, so the sum is $3$.
questions.trick: Each basis dot-itself equals 1, so the sum is simply 3.

questions.q: $(\hat i\times\hat j)+(\hat j\times\hat k)+(\hat k\times\hat i)=$
questions.explanation: $\hat i\times\hat j=\hat k$, $\hat j\times\hat k=\hat i$, $\hat k\times\hat i=\hat j$; summing gives $\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$.
questions.trick: $\hat i\times\hat j+\hat j\times\hat k+\hat k\times\hat i$ cycles to $\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$.

questions.q: The direction ratios of $\vec{AB}$, where $A(1,0,0)$ and $B(0,1,1)$, are
questions.trick: DRs of $\vec{AB}=B-A$, component-wise subtraction, no need to normalise.

questions.q: If $\vec a=2\hat i+3\hat j$, then $|3\vec a|=$
questions.explanation: $|\vec a|=\sqrt{4+9}=\sqrt{13}$, so $|3\vec a|=3\sqrt{13}$.
questions.trick: $|k\vec v|=|k|\cdot|\vec v|$ — pull the scalar out of the magnitude.

questions.q: If $\vec a=2\hat i+\lambda\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i-2\hat j+3\hat k$ are perpendicular, then $\lambda=$
questions.explanation: $\vec a\cdot\vec b=2-2\lambda+3=5-2\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac52$.
questions.trick: Perpendicular $\Rightarrow$ set the dot product to zero and solve for the unknown.

questions.q: The vector equation of the line through the points $(1,2,3)$ and $(4,5,6)$ is
options: $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k)+t(\hat i-\hat j+\hat k)$
$\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k)+t(4\hat i+5\hat j+6\hat k)$
$\vec r=(4\hat i+5\hat j+6\hat k)+t(2\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)$
$\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k)+t(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)$
questions.explanation: Direction $=(4-1,5-2,6-3)=(3,3,3)$, parallel to $(1,1,1)$; the line through $(1,2,3)$ is $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k)+t(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)$.
questions.trick: Direction vector = difference of the two position vectors; use either point in the line.

questions.q: If $|\vec a+\vec b|=|\vec a-\vec b|$ for nonzero vectors $\vec a,\vec b$, then
options: $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are unit vectors
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides: $|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2+2\vec a\cdot\vec b=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2-2\vec a\cdot\vec b\Rightarrow \vec a\cdot\vec b=0$, so they are perpendicular.
questions.trick: Equal magnitudes on both sides forces $\vec a\cdot\vec b=0$ — perpendicular vectors.

questions.q: The vector equation $\vec r=\vec a+t\vec b$ (t a real parameter) represents
options: a straight line through the point with position vector $\vec a$, parallel to $\vec b$
a plane containing the point with position vector $\vec a$
questions.explanation: By definition, this is the vector equation of the straight line through the point with position vector $\vec a$, in the direction of $\vec b$.
questions.trick: $\vec r=\vec a+t\vec b$ is a line through point $\vec a$, direction $\vec b$.

questions.q: $A(0,0,0)$, $B(1,0,0)$, $C(0,1,0)$ are vertices of a triangle. Its area is
questions.explanation: $\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}=(1,0,0)\times(0,1,0)=(0,0,1)$, magnitude 1; area $=\dfrac12(1)=\dfrac12$.
questions.trick: Cross $\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}$, halve the magnitude — works for any 3D triangle.

questions.q: The vectors $2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$, $\hat i+2\hat j-3\hat k$ and $3\hat i+\lambda\hat j+5\hat k$ are coplanar when $\lambda=$
questions.explanation: Setting the scalar triple product $\begin{vmatrix}2&-1&1\\1&2&-3\\3&\lambda&5\end{vmatrix}=0$ gives $28+7\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-4$.
questions.trick: Set the $3\times3$ scalar triple product determinant to zero, solve for the unknown.

questions.q: If $|\vec a|=3$, $|\vec b|=4$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec b=6$, then $|\vec a\times\vec b|=$
questions.explanation: $|\vec a\times\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2-(\vec a\cdot\vec b)^2=144-36=108$, so $|\vec a\times\vec b|=\sqrt{108}=6\sqrt3$.
questions.trick: $|\vec a\times\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2-(\vec a\cdot\vec b)^2$ links dot and cross.

questions.q: A vector perpendicular to both $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j$ and $\vec b=\hat j+\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec a\times\vec b=(1,1,0)\times(0,1,1)=(1,-1,1)=\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$.
questions.trick: A vector perpendicular to two given vectors is exactly their cross product.

questions.q: The work done by a force $\vec F=2\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k$ in producing a displacement $\vec d=\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: Work $=\vec F\cdot\vec d=2-3+2=1$.
questions.trick: Work done by a force $=\vec F\cdot\vec d$ (dot product), never cross product.

questions.q: The volume of the parallelepiped with co-terminous edges $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j$, $\vec b=\hat j+\hat k$, $\vec c=\hat k+\hat i$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec b\times\vec c=(1,1,-1)$; $\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)=(1)(1)+(1)(1)+(0)(-1)=2$, so the volume is $2$.
questions.trick: Volume of a parallelepiped = scalar triple product $\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)$.

questions.q: A unit vector perpendicular to both $\vec a=\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$ and $\vec b=3\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec a\times\vec b=(7,7,-7)$, magnitude $7\sqrt3$; the unit vector is $\dfrac{\hat i+\hat j-\hat k}{\sqrt3}$.
questions.trick: Perpendicular vector = cross product; normalise by dividing by its magnitude.

questions.q: The area of the triangle whose adjacent sides are $\vec a=2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i+2\hat j-3\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec a\times\vec b=(1,7,5)$, magnitude $\sqrt{75}=5\sqrt3$; area $=\dfrac12(5\sqrt3)=\dfrac{5\sqrt3}{2}$.
questions.trick: Area of triangle $=\tfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b|$ — compute cross, take magnitude, halve.

questions.q: For vectors $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$, the value of $(\vec a+\vec b)\cdot[(\vec b+\vec c)\times(\vec c+\vec a)]$ equals
questions.explanation: Expanding using the scalar triple product's multilinearity, all repeated-vector terms vanish, leaving exactly $2[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]$.
questions.trick: This identity always simplifies to exactly $2[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]$ — memorise the factor 2.
